title: 50agents vs Make: canvas or plain words | 50agents
description: Make gives you a visual canvas, 3,500+ apps and blueprints; 50agents builds the automation, AI agent or app from plain words. Every row sourced.
answer: Pick Make if you want to draw and tune every scenario yourself on a visual canvas, with 3,500+ apps, code steps and exportable blueprints.
Pick 50agents if you want to say the job in plain words and approve a tested plan instead of mapping fields; it is free to start.
ask: Set up an automation: every new Shopify order is added as a row to my Google Sheet with its items and total
lede: Make is for builders who want every module in view; 50agents is for people who want the outcome and will check the plan.

us: You want the outcome, not the scenario: a new payment in your sheet, a new lead in Slack.
You need an app with a list, a board and numbers, run by an AI agent, not only a data store.
You want sends to people outside to wait for approval without designing that step.
them: You like building and want control of every module, branch and error handler.
You need code steps, or an app that is in Make's 3,500+ and not in 50agents' 2,300+.
You keep scenarios as blueprints and move them between accounts.

move.title: Export the blueprint
move.body: Save the scenario's blueprint (.json) as your record of every module and mapping.

move.title: Describe the outcome
move.body: Tell Captain what the scenario achieves, not how. It finds the apps, reads a real event and tests the plan on your data.

move.title: Compare, then turn Make off
move.body: Run both for a week, compare the outputs to Make's run history, and switch the scenario off.

faqs.a: For common jobs, yes. For complex hand-built scenarios with nested routers and code, Make is the better tool.

faqs.q: Does 50agents have a visual editor like Make?
faqs.a: It shows every step of an automation, with what each did on a real run, but you change steps by asking in chat, not by dragging modules.
Make: 3,500+ on its homepage. 50agents works with 2,300+ through viaSocket.
